What is the $y$-intercept of the parabola shown above?
question.worked_solution:
First, we need to find the equation of the parabola. From the diagram, we see that the parabola has a vertex at $(2,-5)$ and passes through the point $(-2,3).$

The general standard equation of an up- or down-opening parabola with vertex at $(h,k)$ is given by

$$
(x-h)^{2}=4p(y-k),
$$

and substituting $(h,k)=(2,-5)$ into the above gives

$$
(x-2)^{2}=4p(y+5).
$$

Now, we need to find $p.$ Since the parabola passes through the point $(-2,3),$ we substitute $x=-2$ and $y=3$ into the equation and get

$$
\begin{aligned}(-2-2)^{2} & =4p(3+5) \\ 16 & =4p(8) \\ p & =\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equation of the parabola is

$$
\begin{aligned}(x-2)^{2} & =2(y+5).\end{aligned}
$$

When the parabola intersects the $y$-axis, we must have $x=0.$ So, we substitute $x=0$ into the equation of the parabola and solve for $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}(0-2)^{2} & =2(y+5) \\ 4 & =2(y+5) \\ y & =2-5 \\ y & =-3\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the $y$-intercept is $-3.$
